name: Shemaiah
overview: Shemaiah was a male Levite known as the Nehelamite who prophesied a lie, as recorded in Jeremiah 29. The LORD appointed him priest in place of Jehoiada, confirming his Levitical heritage. His unique role as a false prophet highlights a significant spiritual challenge during his time.
namesAndTitles: The name Shemaiah means 'YHWH hears,' reflecting a proper Hebrew theophoric name. This name is noted in Jeremiah 29:24 but was not given directly by God to this individual.
familyAndRelationships: Shemaiah is inferred to be a descendant of Aaron, the first high priest, establishing his priestly lineage. Additionally, Delaiah is inferred to be his father, connecting him to a known family line within the Levites. Scripture does not provide further family details beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Shemaiah's significance lies in his role as a Levite priest who was appointed by the LORD instead of Jehoiada, marking a shift in priestly authority. However, his prophecy was false, which demonstrates the presence of misleading voices even among the priesthood. His story serves as a cautionary example of the dangers of false prophecy within God's chosen people.
